question.rationale: Feed cations can reduce tetracycline absorption, while dosage-form manipulation and device compatibility require review of the exact product and tube. Swallowing instructions do not establish tube compatibility, mixing medicine into formula does not remove cation interactions, and a shared scaffold does not make administration methods interchangeable. Equipment adherence remains a product-specific consideration; the 2021 FDA development draft does not demonstrate tetracycline-specific loss in a particular tube.

section.heading: Separate chelation from equipment adherence
section.body: Feed minerals can complex with tetracyclines and reduce absorption. Review the exact drug and product instructions when coordinating feeds. Equipment adherence is a separate compatibility issue: adsorption means a drug sticks to a surface. The FDA's June 2021 draft on enteral-tube testing identifies possible adherence of active or inactive ingredients to tube material and proposes measuring how much of a prepared dose reaches the tube outlet. It is a nonbinding development proposal, not a clinical demonstration of tetracycline adsorption in a named tube. Retain this possible mechanism as a product-specific question. Review the formulation, tube site and material, preparation, flushing, and administration instructions. Swallowing instructions or a shared antibiotic scaffold do not establish feeding-tube compatibility.
